Subject: DPA: breach notification timing & cooperation expectations

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the updated DPA redline. Our security and legal teams flagged the incident response / breach notification section — specifically the timing and cooperation language. Under GDPR we need notification to be ‘without undue delay and not later than 72 hours’ to supervisory authorities; our procurement folks want to see how Redwood proposes to mirror that standard contractually.

Two specific asks:
- Can Redwood commit to notifying Acme Health of a confirmed data breach affecting our data within 72 hours of becoming aware?
- We also need clarity around the level of cooperation (forensics access, log preservation, customer notifications, regulator coordination).

Attached our preferred language as a starting point. Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,

Quick notes:

- For suspected incidents, we typically notify that an investigation is underway and provide a follow-up with confirmed scope.

Marcus — can you propose 1–2 options (GDPR-aligned and commercial compromise) and include cooperation wording (log access, root-cause support, public communications coordination)? Evelyn — please flag any operational boundaries (SLA for forensic results, escalation path).

Monica / Sarah — following up with proposed clause text and implementation notes. I’ve attached a DOCX with marked options.

PROPOSED LANGUAGE (Option A — GDPR-aligned):
""
1) Notification: Processor (Redwood) shall notify Controller (Acme Health) of any personal data breach affecting Controller’s data without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than seventy-two (72) hours after becoming aware of the breach. Notification shall include, to the extent reasonably available, a description of the nature and scope of the breach, categories of data affected, likely consequences, measures taken or proposed to address and mitigate the breach, and contact details for the Processor’s incident response lead.
""

PROPOSED LANGUAGE (Option B — commercial compromise):
""
1) Notification: Processor shall notify Controller of any confirmed personal data breach affecting Controller’s data as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event no later than five (5) calendar days after the Processor becomes aware of the breach. Initial notification will indicate whether the incident is under investigation and will be followed by substantive updates as more information becomes available.
""

COOPERATION / INVESTIGATION SUPPORT:
""
2) Upon request, the Processor will: (a) provide reasonable access to forensic findings, logs, and metadata relevant to the incident; (b) preserve evidence for a commercially reasonable period; (c) coordinate with Controller regarding notifications to affected individuals and supervisory authorities; and (d) make available technical and operational personnel for up to ten (10) hours of remote support at no additional cost to assist with Controller’s investigation, with additional time billed at the Processor’s published rates.
""

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES / RISK CALL-OUTS (Evelyn, feel free to edit):
- 72 hours is feasible for confirmed breaches where incident detection and triage establish impact quickly; however, complex incidents that require third-party forensic engagement may need initial notification + follow-up cadence.
- Access to logs may be subject to data minimization and privacy restrictions; we can provide sanitized logs or scoped extracts where full log dumps are not permissible.
- We recommend adding explicit language that Processor’s obligations do not require disclosure of trade secrets or internal security methods.

Attachments: proposed-incident-clause.docx, SOC2-snapshot-2025.pdf

Let me know which option Acme prefers or if they want a hybrid (72-hour initial notification + 5-day contractual window for final scope confirmation).

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Marcus / Monica — appreciate the clear options. Acme’s position is: we need contractual certainty that initial notification will not be delayed. Our procurement/legal team will accept Option A (72 hours) but with a tweak: we require that Redwood provide an initial substantive notification within 48 hours of becoming aware where feasible for incidents that materially impact health data or PII of more than 5,000 individuals. For smaller incidents, 72 hours is acceptable.

On cooperation: the proposed cooperation language looks good; please remove any ambiguity around ‘commercially reasonable period’ for evidence preservation — we prefer a minimum preservation of 90 days unless a legal hold or regulator requires longer.

Can Redwood confirm this 48/72 split and the 90-day preservation baseline? If so, we can move to final redlines.

Regards,
Sarah Patel
Legal Counsel, Acme Health

Attachment: none

Sarah — thanks for the clear direction. I spoke with Marcus and Evelyn this morning. Summary / next steps: 

- Redwood is willing to accept a hybrid approach: initial substantive notification within forty-eight (48) hours for incidents materially affecting >5,000 individuals or involving regulated health data, and otherwise within seventy-two (72) hours of becoming aware.
- Redwood will commit to preserving relevant evidence and forensic artifacts for a minimum of ninety (90) days, unless a regulator or court requires a longer retention period. We will add a carve-out that we will not be required to disclose trade secrets or internal security tooling details.
- Marcus will incorporate the agreed language into the DPA redline and send a final version for Acme review today. Evelyn will prepare a short operational note describing our incident notification cadence (initial notice, 48/72-hour windows, 7-day and 30-day substantive updates).

If that matches Acme’s expectation, we’ll circulate the updated DPA and aim for signature next week. Happy to set up a 30-minute call if you’d prefer to walk through live.
